iOS version is very well-crafted, but the type on iPad Mini is much, much too small.
I've been using this for about a year. It's very polished and been stable for me. The Apple and Android apps work well too... I'm using it as a very basic note system, nothing fancy.

(Notion employee) The Anytype model is really cool - they've rebuilt Lotus Notes with 21st century E2E encrypted protocols. But it's been work-in-progress since 2019 and still lacks collaboration and a browser version, putting it in a smaller PKM market.

i've been following anytype since 2019... it has transitioned from being a libp2p based google docs alternative into something more complicated, with relationships, sets, etc, and tbh i just never use it, because it's become too complicated.

In contrast with many others crappy things (Notion, Standard Notes, Joplin, Notesnook, Obsidian, etc), Anytype is, at least, barely acceptable... The UX isn't that nice at this point (especially the graph view which is totally useless if you have at least hundreds of objects).
Why does this smell like a cult?... And why do I need to login for an offline app? Where does the data really go?... Seems there is no way to really access or control my files externally.
I've been on the waitlist to try this for close to 5 years and never once received an email... it is too similar to Notion for my taste... I'll stick with Obsidian because I value the flexibility.

Painful to import things from Logseq or Obsidian. It imports one md at a time, and the 'zip' thing does not click me... The P2P sync is what made me try in the first place. It's working fine, nice!...Unusable for my own backup purposes.

Very nice and well developed product. I've been using it for a while! Glad that it's public and has a mobile app now! I've been a heavy user of Notion, finally, there is a better and more secured alternative!

I've been using this heavily, it's a good tool... Anytype feels joyful to use in a similar way to Notion but without weight of Notion's mountain of features... There's some QoL issues present which annoy me, but they're nitpicks at best.

I tried this briefly about a year ago but didn't see myself using it. They had an hour long induction session over zoom to teach how to use the tool before they sent the download link... It was too complicated. Moved on to Zotero and text/plain files.
Note, their idea of 'open source' doesn't match the popular Open Source Definition (linking to their license).
Compared to Obsidian, I can't just use raw Markdown or CSV file with Anytype. I've paid Obsidian $300+ just because it's data independence with a few obvious strings attached.
(co-founder) We don't offer a browser version. Instead, we have an Electron-based cross-platform app that works on Windows, Linux, and macOS. We also have two native mobile apps for iOS and Android.

I found Anytype a few months ago and thought 'wow maybe I can ditch Turtl and just use this.' A few things bugged me: it's a source-available license; you can't share with others yet; they call it e2e encrypted, but all your data lives unencrypted on-disk... That said, I think the interface and utility of the tool are amazing.

(co-founder) All your data in Anytype is encrypted at rest; only the indexes of this data are not encrypted. We have plans to also encrypt the indexes... Our protocol is p2p and it's already working well in local networks.
Anytype is in closed alpha with 8,000 currently testing it. You can try it yourself using the invite code - hn. Please remember it's an early alfa which doesn't have a proper onboarding.
The scrolling banner screams 'this is a scam' to me for some reason. And that's not even touching the weirdness of that manifesto. But, other than that, I hope it exists.
I've applied for an invite more than 2 years ago - still got nothing! This looks like an email honeypot!
